result.title: Guarding with Judgment: Learning to Intervene for Multimodal Safety
result.summary: When visual context makes an ordinary request unsafe to answer as asked, a blanket refusal may leave the user's need unresolved. Choosing how to help requires distinguishing an established hazard from a condition that still needs verification, a distinction that binary safety labels leave unspecified. We formulate this decision through four actions: allow, warn, review, and refuse. To ground these decisions in verifiable evidence, we build a corpus of 20,126 training audits and the JudiBench benchmark, connecting each action to diagnostic judgments, source evidence, and controlled context changes. Our guard, JudiAct, separately states what the source establishes, what condition governs the help, and how the rules apply. It then checks these three brief review items against the original inputs to predict diagnostic labels and a handling action. Supervised training learns individual judgments while comparing label assignments across related cases. A second stage swaps one review item at a time, using the resulting audit feedback to refine review generation. On JudiBench, JudiAct improves request and answer Macro-F1 by more than 28 percentage points over its 4B backbone. Across nine public benchmarks, it outperforms state-of-the-art guards on the mean delivered-answer score in both pre-generation and post-generation settings, cutting MM-SafetyBench attack success from 40.78% to 25.30%.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究多模态安全场景下应「如何干预」而非一律拒答：构建约两万条审计语料与 JudiBench 基准，提出 JudiAct 分别陈述证据确立的内容、适用条件与规则适用三条审查项，并借逐项替换审查项获得的反馈精炼判断，最终输出 allow/warn/review/refuse 四类动作。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「已确立风险」与「仍待核实条件」的动作区分及证据审计机制，可能为视觉证据充分性判断与 THINK/LOOK/STOP 式干预决策提供线索，审查项替换也可供核查贡献分配与视觉旁路；但该方法为独立 guard 分类器，未涉及 latent 推理状态，迁移价值需读原文确认。
